intro: In B2 you learnt to take part in meetings: interrupt politely, clarify, sum up and give a progress update. Now you're in the chair. You'll open a meeting and set the agenda, keep the discussion fair and on track, calm a disagreement, and guide the group to a clear decision with action points. Warm-up: think of the best meeting you've ever been in. What did the person leading it do?
teachingNotes: This functional lesson builds on b2-meetings (taking part: Sorry to interrupt, but …; Could you clarify what you mean by …?; So what you're saying is …?; So, to sum up, …; progress updates: on track / behind schedule) and on the facilitating part of b2-mediation-data-texts (Our aim today is to …; Dimas, we haven't heard from you yet; Let's come back to it later; We've got five minutes left; So, we've agreed to …). Recap those in a line; don't re-teach them. New here: the learner CHAIRS a real meeting (pemimpin rapat): a formal opening with aim, time, agenda and roles, ground rules for a hybrid meeting (some people in the room, some on Zoom / Teams), stopping someone who dominates, parking off-topic points, handling conflict, steering to a decision (consensus or a vote) and closing with action points. Contexts: a bank in Surabaya, a startup in Jakarta, an NGO in Yogyakarta, partners joining from Singapore, Pak Hasan and Bu Ani as senior managers.

Opening: Thanks for coming, everyone. Let's make a start. (make a start is more British; Let's get started works everywhere) / The aim of today's meeting is to … / We've got 45 minutes and three items on the agenda. / Could Sari take the minutes? (the minutes = notulen, the official record; here minutes doesn't mean menit; 'notulen' isn't English) / Could Dimas keep an eye on the time? Hybrid ground rules: For those joining online, please stay on mute when you're not speaking. / If you'd like to speak, use the raise-hand button. / I'll keep an eye on the chat. Common errors: *Let's we start (from 'Mari kita mulai') → Let's start; *We will discuss about … → discuss (no about); waiting 15 minutes for latecomers (jam karet) while online partners sit in an empty call → start on time: Let's make a start, and we'll fill Budi in when he arrives (fill someone in = tell them what they missed: a phrase to remember).

Managing the discussion: quiet people by name and with a reason (Dimas, we haven't heard from you yet. You know the client: what's your view?), never calling someone out (*Why are you so quiet?); someone dominating: thank, then open the floor (Thanks, Budi. I'd like to hear from others too.), not *Budi, you talk too much / *Stop, Budi; off topic: That's a valid point, but it's not on today's agenda. Can we park it? (park = set aside for later, like parking a car; some teams keep a 'parking lot' list; avoid 'table it', which means postpone in American English but discuss now in British English); time: We've got five minutes left on this item. / Let's move on to the next item. / Let's give this five more minutes, then decide. Conflict: I can see you both feel strongly about this. / Let's separate the two issues. / What do we agree on? / Let's focus on the issue, not the person. / Let's take that offline. Trap: in Indonesian 'offline' means luring / tatap muka, but 'take it offline' means discuss it later, separately, with only the people involved (it can even happen on Zoom). Too harsh: *Stop arguing! / *You're both wrong.

Steering to a decision: summarise the positions fairly, with names and reasons (So, there are two views. Rina prefers … because …; Budi would rather … because …), without taking sides; propose (So, can we agree to …? / Shall we go with option B? (Should we … is more common in American English) / I suggest we …); check consensus (Can everyone live with that? = can you accept it even if it isn't your favourite / Any objections?) or vote (Let's put it to a vote. / Can I have a show of hands?). Silence is not agreement. Action points = who + what + by when: Rina will send the draft by Thursday. Common errors: vague action points (*We'll follow up / *Someone will check it / *ASAP) and *until Thursday for a deadline (from 'sampai Kamis'): by Thursday = paling lambat Kamis; until = something continues up to that time. Closing: Let's go over the action points. / To sum up, … / Our next meeting is on … / Thanks, everyone. I'll send round the minutes.

Culture, presented with respect: in many Indonesian meetings the start is late, the most senior person speaks first and others don't contradict them (sungkan, ewuh pakewuh), and decisions are made by musyawarah untuk mufakat (discussion until everyone agrees). Musyawarah is a real strength: everyone is heard, the decision is owned by the group and relationships are protected; international teams often call this 'building buy-in'. But it can take several meetings and can hide disagreement, and international teams often expect a decision in this meeting with a clear owner. Bridges for the chair: hear the team before the senior person (Let's hear from the team first, then Pak Hasan.), invite disagreement (Does anyone see it differently?), and agree at the start how you'll decide (We'll aim for consensus, but if we can't agree by eleven, we'll vote / Bu Ani will decide.).

Limits: A0–B2 grammar plus the chain; no inversion, cleft sentences, subjunctive or impersonal passives in examples. Don't teach writing formal minutes, negotiating tactics or presentations. At C1 much of chairing is style: several phrases can work, so only test clear cases (a clearly polite, effective move vs. one that is rude, vague, takes sides or fakes agreement). When the learner practises, play a meeting participant (a dominating Budi, a quiet Dimas, two colleagues arguing), react naturally, then correct ONE thing, usually 'Let's we start', 'until Thursday', a vague action point, 'Why are you so quiet?' or 'offline' misunderstood. Listening items use one voice and no speaker labels.

keyPoints.title: Open the meeting and set the agenda
keyPoints.explanation: Open in four moves: start on time (Thanks for coming, everyone. Let's make a start.), say the aim (The aim of today's meeting is to …), give the time and the agenda (We've got 45 minutes and three items on the agenda.) and give roles and rules (Could Sari take the minutes? For those joining online, please stay on mute and use the raise-hand button.). The minutes = notulen. Say Let's start, not 'Let's we start'.

examples.en: Thanks for coming, everyone. Let's make a start.
examples.id: Terima kasih sudah datang, semuanya. Mari kita mulai.

examples.en: The aim of today's meeting is to choose a supplier for the new uniforms.
examples.id: Tujuan rapat hari ini adalah memilih pemasok untuk seragam baru.

examples.en: For those joining online, please stay on mute when you're not speaking.
examples.id: Untuk yang bergabung online, mohon tetap mute saat tidak berbicara.

id.title: Membuka rapat dan mengatur agenda
id.explanation: Buka rapat dengan empat langkah: mulai tepat waktu (Thanks for coming, everyone. Let's make a start.), sebutkan tujuannya (The aim of today's meeting is to …), sebutkan waktu dan agendanya (We've got 45 minutes and three items on the agenda.) dan bagi peran serta aturannya (Could Sari take the minutes? For those joining online, please stay on mute and use the raise-hand button.). The minutes = notulen. Katakan Let's start, bukan 'Let's we start'.

keyPoints.title: Manage the discussion and handle conflict
keyPoints.explanation: Bring quiet people in by name (Dimas, we haven't heard from you yet.), stop someone dominating politely (Thanks, Budi. I'd like to hear from others too.), park off-topic points (That's a valid point, but it's not on today's agenda. Can we park it?) and keep time (We've got five minutes left on this item.). In a conflict, stay calm and neutral: I can see you both feel strongly about this. / Let's separate the two issues. / What do we agree on? / Let's take that offline (= later, separately, not face to face).

examples.en: Thanks, Budi. I'd like to hear from others too. Sari, what's your view?
examples.id: Terima kasih, Budi. Saya juga ingin mendengar dari yang lain. Sari, bagaimana pandanganmu?

examples.en: That's a valid point, but it's not on today's agenda. Can we park it?
examples.id: Poin yang bagus, tapi itu tidak ada di agenda hari ini. Bisa kita simpan dulu?

examples.en: I can see you both feel strongly about this. What do we agree on?
examples.id: Saya lihat kalian berdua sangat peduli soal ini. Hal apa yang sudah kita sepakati?

id.title: Mengelola diskusi dan menangani konflik
id.explanation: Ajak orang yang pendiam bicara dengan menyebut namanya (Dimas, we haven't heard from you yet.), hentikan orang yang menguasai pembicaraan dengan sopan (Thanks, Budi. I'd like to hear from others too.), simpan dulu poin di luar topik (That's a valid point, but it's not on today's agenda. Can we park it?) dan jaga waktu (We've got five minutes left on this item.). Saat ada konflik, tetap tenang dan netral: I can see you both feel strongly about this. / Let's separate the two issues. / What do we agree on? / Let's take that offline (= dibahas nanti, terpisah, bukan berarti tatap muka).

keyPoints.title: Steer to a decision and agree next steps
keyPoints.explanation: Summarise the positions fairly, with names and reasons (So, there are two views: …). Then propose (So, can we agree to …? / Shall we go with option B?) and check: consensus (Can everyone live with that? / Any objections?) or a vote (Let's put it to a vote.). Silence isn't agreement. Each action point needs who + what + by when: Rina will send the draft by Thursday (by = paling lambat, not until). Close with To sum up, … and the date of the next meeting.

examples.en: So, can we agree to launch the campaign in April?
examples.id: Jadi, bisakah kita sepakat meluncurkan kampanyenya bulan April?

examples.en: Rina will send the draft by Thursday.
examples.id: Rina akan mengirim drafnya paling lambat hari Kamis.

id.title: Mengarahkan ke keputusan dan menyepakati langkah berikutnya
id.explanation: Rangkum posisi masing-masing dengan adil, lengkap dengan nama dan alasannya (So, there are two views: …). Lalu usulkan (So, can we agree to …? / Shall we go with option B?) dan cek: mufakat (Can everyone live with that? / Any objections?) atau voting (Let's put it to a vote.). Diam bukan berarti setuju. Setiap poin tindak lanjut butuh siapa + apa + paling lambat kapan: Rina will send the draft by Thursday (by = paling lambat, bukan until). Tutup dengan To sum up, … dan tanggal rapat berikutnya.

guidedPractice.prompt: You're opening a 45-minute meeting. Complete with one word: We've got 45 minutes and three ___ on the agenda.
Half the team is on Zoom. Set a ground rule. Complete with one word: For those joining online, please stay on ___ when you're not speaking.
guidedPractice.hint: The microphone is off: you're on …

guidedPractice.prompt: Dimas hasn't said anything for 30 minutes. Bring him in. Complete with one word: Dimas, we haven't ___ from you yet. What do you think?
guidedPractice.hint: hear in the present perfect: we haven't …

guidedPractice.prompt: Only ten minutes remain for this item. Complete with one word: We've got ten minutes ___ on this item, so let's start moving towards a decision.
Propose a decision as a question. Complete with one word: So, can we ___ to launch the campaign in April?

independentPractice.prompt: Two colleagues are arguing about the budget and the timeline at the same time. Complete with one word: Let's ___ the two issues: first the budget, then the timeline.
Not everyone loves the plan, but you want to check that everyone can accept it. Complete with one word: Can everyone ___ with that?
independentPractice.hint: A phrase to remember: … with something = accept it, even if it isn't your favourite.

independentPractice.prompt: Propose option B as a question. Complete with one word: ___ we go with option B?
independentPractice.hint: A word for suggestions: … we start?

assessment.prompt: You're chairing a budget meeting at a bank in Surabaya. After welcoming everyone, you say what the meeting is for. Complete with one word: The ___ of today's meeting is to agree on next year's training budget.
assessment.rubric: Correct: aim (The aim of today's meeting is to … = tujuan rapat hari ini). 'purpose', 'goal' and 'objective' are also correct = 100. 'point' = 80 (natural in speech, a bit informal). 'focus' = 70 (understood, but 'the focus … is to agree' is less natural). 'aims' = 70 (one meeting, one aim: The aim … is). 'target' = 50. 'agenda' = 30 (the agenda is the list of items, not the goal).

assessment.prompt: The meeting is about to start, and someone needs to write the official record of what's discussed and decided (notulen). Ask Sari politely. Complete with one word: Could Sari take the ___?
assessment.rubric: Correct: minutes (take the minutes = mencatat notulen; here minutes doesn't mean menit). 'notes' = 70 (understood and fine in an informal team, but the official record is the minutes). 'minute' = 60 (the record is always plural: the minutes). 'note' = 40. 'notulen' / 'notula' = 0 (Indonesian, not English).

assessment.prompt: In a meeting about the new office layout in Bandung, Budi starts talking about salary increases. It matters, but it isn't on today's agenda. Complete with one word (it's also what you do with a car): That's a valid point, Budi, but it's not on today's agenda. Can we ___ it for now and come back to it next month?
assessment.rubric: Correct: park (park it = set it aside for later, like parking a car). 'leave', 'save' or 'hold' = 80 (good English, but the clue asks for the car word, the chair's set phrase). 'table' = 50 (it means postpone in American English but discuss now in British English: avoid it in international meetings). 'parking' = 50 (after can we, use the base form). 'skip' = 40 (skip means leaving it out, not coming back to it). 'stop' = 30.

assessment.prompt: In a team meeting, Rina and Dimas start arguing about one invoice from August. Only the two of them need to sort it out, and eight people are waiting. Complete with one word: I can see you both feel strongly about this. Let's take that ___ and discuss it after the meeting.
assessment.rubric: Correct: offline (take that offline = discuss it later, separately, with only the people involved; it has nothing to do with meeting face to face). 'outside' = 40. 'off' = 40. 'later' = 30 ('take that later' isn't the phrase, although 'Let's discuss that later' is fine as a different sentence). 'online' = 0 (the opposite word).

assessment.prompt: Pak Hasan needs the signed contract on Thursday at the latest (paling lambat). Complete the action point with one word: Budi will send Pak Hasan the signed contract ___ Thursday.
assessment.rubric: Correct: by (by Thursday = paling lambat hari Kamis: a deadline). 'before' = 70 (understood, but strictly it means by Wednesday). 'on' = 60 (a fixed day, not a deadline). 'until' / 'till' = 20 (a common trap from 'sampai Kamis': until is for something that continues up to that time). 'at' = 10.

assessment.prompt: This action point is in the minutes of a project meeting in Jakarta: 'Budi will call the supplier about the late delivery.' Bu Ani says it's incomplete. A good action point says who, what and by when. Which one is missing here? Write one word: who, what or when.
assessment.rubric: Correct: when (there is a who, Budi, and a what, call the supplier, but no deadline, e.g. by Wednesday). 'by when' / 'deadline' = 100. 'date' / 'time' = 80 (the right idea). 'who' = 0 (Budi is the who). 'what' = 0 (calling the supplier about the delivery is the what).

assessment.prompt: At the end of the meeting, you repeat the decisions in a few words before you close. Complete with one word: To ___ up: we've chosen the venue in Bandung, Sari will book it by Friday, and our next meeting is on the 3rd.
assessment.rubric: Correct: sum (To sum up = sebagai rangkuman). 'wrap' (To wrap up) = 100. 'some' = 70 (heard right, spelled wrong). 'summarise' / 'summarize' = 50 (a good verb, but it doesn't take 'up': To summarise, …). 'conclude' = 40. 'close' = 30.

material.title: Opening the meeting and setting the agenda

blocks.text:
Quick recap: in B2 you **took part** in meetings: you interrupted politely (*Sorry to interrupt, but …*), clarified, summed up and gave updates. You also led group work: *Our aim today is to …*, *Dimas, we haven't heard from you yet.* Now you're the **chair** (pemimpin rapat): the person who opens the meeting, keeps it on track and gets a decision.

The first minute sets the tone. Open in four moves:
- **Start on time:** ***Thanks for coming, everyone. Let's make a start.*** (*make a start* is more British; ***Let's get started*** works everywhere.)
- **Say the aim:** ***The aim of today's meeting is to …*** (*aim* = tujuan: what you want to have at the end, e.g. a decision).
- **Time and agenda** (agenda = the list of topics, each one is an **item**): ***We've got 45 minutes and three items on the agenda.***
- **Roles:** ***Could Sari take the minutes?*** (**the minutes** = notulen, the official record) / ***Could Dimas keep an eye on the time?*** (keep an eye on = memantau)

In a **hybrid** meeting (some people in the room, some on Zoom or Teams), add **ground rules** (aturan main): ***For those joining online, please stay on mute when you're not speaking.*** / ***If you'd like to speak, use the raise-hand button.*** / ***I'll keep an eye on the chat.***

id.text:
Rekap singkat: di B2 kamu **ikut serta** dalam rapat: menyela dengan sopan (*Sorry to interrupt, but …*), mengklarifikasi, merangkum dan memberi update. Kamu juga sudah memandu kerja kelompok: *Our aim today is to …*, *Dimas, we haven't heard from you yet.* Sekarang kamu **chair** (pemimpin rapat): orang yang membuka rapat, menjaganya tetap fokus dan menghasilkan keputusan.

Menit pertama menentukan suasananya. Buka dengan empat langkah:
- **Mulai tepat waktu:** ***Thanks for coming, everyone. Let's make a start.*** (*make a start* lebih British; ***Let's get started*** cocok di mana saja.)
- **Sebutkan tujuannya:** ***The aim of today's meeting is to …*** (*aim* = tujuan: apa yang ingin kalian dapat di akhir, misalnya sebuah keputusan).
- **Waktu dan agenda** (agenda = daftar topik, setiap topik disebut **item** atau butir): ***We've got 45 minutes and three items on the agenda.***
- **Peran:** ***Could Sari take the minutes?*** (**the minutes** = notulen, catatan resmi rapat) / ***Could Dimas keep an eye on the time?*** (keep an eye on = memantau)

Di rapat **hybrid** (sebagian di ruangan, sebagian di Zoom atau Teams), tambahkan **aturan main** (ground rules): ***For those joining online, please stay on mute when you're not speaking.*** / ***If you'd like to speak, use the raise-hand button.*** / ***I'll keep an eye on the chat.***

rows.en: Thanks for coming, everyone. Let's make a start.
rows.id: Terima kasih sudah datang, semuanya. Mari kita mulai.

rows.en: The aim of today's meeting is to agree on the launch date.
rows.id: Tujuan rapat hari ini adalah menyepakati tanggal peluncuran.

rows.en: We've got an hour and four items on the agenda.
rows.id: Kita punya waktu satu jam dan empat butir agenda.

rows.en: Could Sari take the minutes, and could Dimas keep an eye on the time?
rows.id: Bisakah Sari mencatat notulennya, dan Dimas memantau waktunya?

rows.en: For those joining online, please use the raise-hand button if you'd like to speak.
rows.id: Untuk yang bergabung online, silakan pakai tombol angkat tangan kalau ingin bicara.

rows.en: Let's make a start, and we'll fill Budi in when he arrives.
rows.id: Mari kita mulai, nanti kita ceritakan ke Budi saat dia datang.
rows.note: fill someone in = tell them what they missed (a phrase to remember)

id.note: fill someone in = menceritakan apa yang dia lewatkan (ungkapan untuk dihafal)

blocks.text:
Three Indonesian traps:
- **`Let's we start` ✗** (from *Mari kita mulai*). *Let's* already means *let us*, so don't add *we*: **Let's start.** / **Let's make a start.** And **discuss** has no *about*: *We'll discuss the budget*, not `discuss about the budget` ✗.
- **minutes ≠ menit here.** *Take the minutes* = mencatat notulen. *Notulen* isn't English, and the minute-taker is simply *the person taking the minutes*.
- **Jam karet.** In many Indonesian offices the meeting starts when the boss or most people arrive. International partners usually expect you to start on time, and in a hybrid meeting the people online are sitting in an empty call. Start, and **fill the latecomers in** afterwards.

id.text:
Tiga jebakan untuk orang Indonesia:
- **`Let's we start` ✗** (dari *Mari kita mulai*). *Let's* sudah berarti *let us*, jadi jangan tambah *we*: **Let's start.** / **Let's make a start.** Dan **discuss** tidak pakai *about*: *We'll discuss the budget*, bukan `discuss about the budget` ✗.
- **minutes di sini ≠ menit.** *Take the minutes* = mencatat notulen. *Notulen* bukan bahasa Inggris, dan notulisnya cukup disebut *the person taking the minutes*.
- **Jam karet.** Di banyak kantor di Indonesia, rapat dimulai saat atasan atau kebanyakan orang sudah datang. Mitra internasional biasanya berharap rapat mulai tepat waktu, dan di rapat hybrid, peserta online sedang menunggu di panggilan yang kosong. Mulai saja, lalu **ceritakan ke yang terlambat** (fill them in) setelahnya.

blocks.prompt: It's 2 p.m., the start time. Two colleagues are still on their way, and partners from Singapore are already waiting on Zoom. What's the best thing to say?
options: Let's we wait for the others, maybe fifteen minutes more.
Okay. Meeting. Item one: the budget.
Thanks for coming, everyone. Let's make a start, and we'll fill the others in when they arrive.
blocks.explain: The chair starts on time, welcomes people and promises to update the latecomers (*fill the others in*). The first option keeps the partners waiting and has the *Let's we* error; the second has no welcome, no aim and sounds rude.

id.prompt: Sekarang jam 2 siang, jam mulainya. Dua rekan masih di jalan, dan mitra dari Singapura sudah menunggu di Zoom. Apa yang paling baik diucapkan?
id.explain: Chair mulai tepat waktu, menyapa peserta dan berjanji memberi tahu yang terlambat (*fill the others in*). Pilihan pertama membuat mitra menunggu dan ada kesalahan *Let's we*; pilihan kedua tanpa sapaan, tanpa tujuan dan terdengar kasar.

material.title: Managing the discussion: quiet voices, long speakers, the agenda and the clock

id.title: Mengelola diskusi: yang pendiam, yang bicara terlalu lama, agenda dan waktu

blocks.text:
Once the discussion is running, the chair makes sure everyone is heard, nobody takes over, and the meeting stays on the agenda and on time.
- **Bring in quiet people** by name, with a reason: ***Dimas, we haven't heard from you yet. You know the client: what's your view?*** / ***Does anyone see it differently?***
- **Stop someone dominating** (menguasai pembicaraan): thank them first, then open the floor: ***Thanks, Budi. I'd like to hear from others too.*** / ***Let's hear from someone who hasn't spoken yet.***
- **Keep on track:** ***That's a valid point, but it's not on today's agenda. Can we park it?*** (**park** = parkir: set it aside and come back to it later; some teams write these points on a list called a *parking lot*) / ***Let's get back to the agenda.***
- **Keep time:** ***We've got five minutes left on this item.*** / ***Let's give this five more minutes, then decide.*** / ***Let's move on to the next item.***

id.text:
Begitu diskusi berjalan, chair memastikan semua orang didengar, tidak ada yang menguasai pembicaraan, dan rapat tetap sesuai agenda dan waktu.
- **Ajak orang yang pendiam** dengan menyebut namanya dan alasannya: ***Dimas, we haven't heard from you yet. You know the client: what's your view?*** / ***Does anyone see it differently?***
- **Hentikan orang yang mendominasi** (menguasai pembicaraan): ucapkan terima kasih dulu, lalu buka kesempatan untuk yang lain: ***Thanks, Budi. I'd like to hear from others too.*** / ***Let's hear from someone who hasn't spoken yet.***
- **Jaga tetap fokus:** ***That's a valid point, but it's not on today's agenda. Can we park it?*** (**park** = parkir: sisihkan dulu, nanti dibahas lagi; ada tim yang menulis poin-poin ini di daftar bernama *parking lot*) / ***Let's get back to the agenda.***
- **Jaga waktu:** ***We've got five minutes left on this item.*** / ***Let's give this five more minutes, then decide.*** / ***Let's move on to the next item.***

rows.en: Dimas, we haven't heard from you yet. You've worked with this supplier: what do you think?
rows.id: Dimas, kami belum mendengar pendapatmu. Kamu pernah bekerja dengan pemasok ini: bagaimana menurutmu?

rows.en: Thanks, Budi, that's really helpful. I'd like to hear from others too.
rows.id: Terima kasih, Budi, itu sangat membantu. Saya juga ingin mendengar dari yang lain.

rows.en: That's a valid point, but it's not on today's agenda. Can we park it and come back to it next week?
rows.id: Poin yang bagus, tapi itu tidak ada di agenda hari ini. Bisa kita simpan dulu dan bahas lagi minggu depan?

rows.en: We're running short of time, so let's move on to item three.
rows.id: Waktu kita mulai habis, jadi mari lanjut ke butir ketiga.

rows.en: Let's hear from the team first, and then Pak Hasan.
rows.id: Mari kita dengar dari tim dulu, lalu dari Pak Hasan.
rows.note: a polite way to stop the senior person's view from ending the discussion

id.note: cara sopan supaya pendapat atasan tidak langsung menutup diskusi

blocks.text:
Two habits to watch:
- **Calling people out.** `Why are you so quiet?` ✗ or `Budi, you talk too much` ✗ embarrass people in front of everyone. Invite by name with a reason, and thank before you move on. Avoid `table it` for 'postpone': in American English it means postpone, but in British English it means *discuss now*. **Park it** is clear to everyone.
- **The senior person speaks first.** In many Indonesian meetings, Pak or Bu (the most senior person) gives their view first, and after that nobody contradicts them (sungkan). The meeting then only confirms one opinion. As chair, ask the team first (*Let's hear from the team first, then Pak Hasan.*) and invite disagreement openly (*Does anyone see it differently? What could go wrong?*).

id.text:
Dua kebiasaan yang perlu diperhatikan:
- **Mempermalukan orang.** `Why are you so quiet?` ✗ atau `Budi, you talk too much` ✗ membuat orang malu di depan semua orang. Ajak dengan menyebut nama dan alasannya, dan ucapkan terima kasih sebelum pindah ke orang lain. Hindari `table it` untuk 'menunda': di bahasa Inggris Amerika artinya menunda, tapi di bahasa Inggris British artinya *membahas sekarang*. **Park it** jelas bagi semua orang.
- **Atasan bicara duluan.** Di banyak rapat di Indonesia, Pak atau Bu (orang paling senior) menyampaikan pendapat lebih dulu, dan setelah itu tidak ada yang membantah (sungkan). Rapatnya jadi hanya mengiyakan satu pendapat. Sebagai chair, tanya tim lebih dulu (*Let's hear from the team first, then Pak Hasan.*) dan undang perbedaan pendapat secara terbuka (*Does anyone see it differently? What could go wrong?*).

blocks.prompt: In a team meeting, Sari hasn't said anything for half an hour, but she knows the client better than anyone. What's the best way to bring her in?
options: Sari, why are you so quiet today?
Sari, we haven't heard from you yet. You know the client best: what's your view?
Anyone else? No? OK, next item.
blocks.explain: It invites Sari by name and gives a reason (*You know the client best*), so she feels valued, not judged. *Why are you so quiet?* puts her on the spot, and *Anyone else? No?* lets the quiet people stay quiet.

id.prompt: Dalam rapat tim, Sari belum bicara sama sekali selama setengah jam, padahal dia paling kenal kliennya. Apa cara terbaik untuk mengajaknya bicara?
id.explain: Kalimat ini mengajak Sari dengan menyebut namanya dan memberi alasan (*You know the client best*), jadi dia merasa dihargai, bukan dihakimi. *Why are you so quiet?* menyudutkannya, dan *Anyone else? No?* membiarkan yang pendiam tetap diam.

blocks.text:
Disagreement is healthy: it's how a team finds the best option. A fight isn't. The chair keeps the discussion about the **issue**, not the **people**, and stays neutral (doesn't take sides). Four moves:
- **Name the feeling, calmly:** ***I can see you both feel strongly about this.***
- **Separate the issues:** often two problems are mixed up: ***Let's separate the two issues: first the launch date, then the budget.***
- **Find common ground** (titik temu): ***What do we agree on?*** / ***We all want the launch to go well.***
- **Move a side argument out of the meeting:** ***Let's take that offline.*** = let's discuss it later, separately, with only the people involved.

Also useful: ***Let's focus on the issue, not the person.*** / ***Let's hear both sides first.***

id.text:
Perbedaan pendapat itu sehat: dari situ tim menemukan pilihan terbaik. Pertengkaran tidak. Chair menjaga diskusi tetap tentang **masalahnya**, bukan **orangnya**, dan tetap netral (tidak memihak). Empat langkah:
- **Sebutkan perasaannya dengan tenang:** ***I can see you both feel strongly about this.***
- **Pisahkan masalahnya:** sering dua masalah tercampur: ***Let's separate the two issues: first the launch date, then the budget.***
- **Cari titik temu:** ***What do we agree on?*** / ***We all want the launch to go well.***
- **Bawa perdebatan sampingan keluar dari rapat:** ***Let's take that offline.*** = mari kita bahas nanti, terpisah, hanya dengan orang yang terlibat.

Juga berguna: ***Let's focus on the issue, not the person.*** / ***Let's hear both sides first.***

rows.en: I can see you both feel strongly about this. Let's hear both sides first.
rows.id: Saya lihat kalian berdua sangat peduli soal ini. Mari dengar kedua pihak dulu.

rows.en: Let's separate the two issues: the price and the delivery date.
rows.id: Mari kita pisahkan dua masalahnya: harga dan tanggal pengiriman.

rows.en: OK, what do we agree on? We all want the client to stay with us.
rows.id: Oke, apa yang sudah kita sepakati? Kita semua ingin klien tetap bersama kita.

rows.en: That's a question for Rina and Dimas. Let's take that offline.
rows.id: Itu urusan Rina dan Dimas. Kita bahas itu terpisah, di luar rapat.
rows.note: offline here = outside this meeting, not face to face

id.note: offline di sini = di luar rapat ini, bukan tatap muka

rows.en: Let's focus on the issue, not the person.
rows.id: Mari fokus pada masalahnya, bukan orangnya.

blocks.text:
**`offline` ≠ luring here.** In Indonesian, *rapat offline* means a face-to-face meeting. But in a meeting, ***Let's take that offline*** means *let's discuss it later, separately, outside this meeting*: it can even happen on Zoom! So don't answer *Sure, I'll come to your office*; answer ***Sure, let's talk after the meeting.***

Too harsh for a chair: `Stop arguing!` ✗, `You're both wrong.` ✗, `Rina, you're being emotional.` ✗. These make the conflict about people. Name the feeling, then turn to the issue.

id.text:
**`offline` di sini ≠ luring.** Dalam bahasa Indonesia, *rapat offline* berarti rapat tatap muka. Tapi dalam rapat, ***Let's take that offline*** berarti *mari kita bahas nanti, terpisah, di luar rapat ini*: bahkan bisa lewat Zoom! Jadi jangan jawab *Sure, I'll come to your office*; jawab ***Sure, let's talk after the meeting.***

Terlalu keras untuk seorang chair: `Stop arguing!` ✗, `You're both wrong.` ✗, `Rina, you're being emotional.` ✗. Kalimat seperti ini membuat konfliknya jadi soal orang. Sebutkan perasaannya, lalu kembali ke masalahnya.

blocks.prompt: Your Indonesian colleague hears the chair say 'Let's take that offline' and thinks it means a face-to-face meeting. What does it actually mean?
options: Let's discuss it later, separately, with only the people involved.
Let's turn off the Zoom call and meet in the office.
Let's never discuss that topic again.
blocks.explain: *Take something offline* = move it out of the meeting and discuss it later with only the people involved. It's about *where* the discussion happens (not in this meeting), not about the internet or meeting in person, and the topic isn't cancelled.

id.prompt: Rekanmu mendengar chair berkata 'Let's take that offline' dan mengira artinya rapat tatap muka. Sebenarnya apa artinya?
id.explain: *Take something offline* = membawanya keluar dari rapat dan membahasnya nanti hanya dengan orang yang terlibat. Ini soal *di mana* diskusinya terjadi (tidak di rapat ini), bukan soal internet atau bertemu langsung, dan topiknya tidak dibatalkan.
options: Bahas nanti secara terpisah, hanya dengan orang yang terlibat.
Matikan Zoom dan bertemu di kantor.
Jangan pernah membahas topik itu lagi.

blocks.text:
When the group has talked enough, the chair guides it to a decision in three steps.
- **Summarise the positions** fairly, with names and reasons, without taking sides: ***So, there are two views. Rina prefers an online launch because it's cheaper; Budi would rather launch in Jakarta because the client wants an event.***
- **Propose:** ***So, can we agree to …?*** / ***Shall we go with option B?*** (*Shall we* is more British; Americans often say ***Should we …?***) / ***I suggest we …***
- **Check the decision:** by **consensus** (everyone accepts it): ***Can everyone live with that?*** (= can you accept it, even if it isn't your favourite) / ***Any objections?*** Or by a **vote** (pemungutan suara): ***Let's put it to a vote.*** / ***Can I have a show of hands?***

Remember from B2: **silence isn't agreement.** If nobody speaks, ask again, or ask the quiet people by name.

id.text:
Kalau kelompok sudah cukup berdiskusi, chair mengarahkannya ke sebuah keputusan dalam tiga langkah.
- **Rangkum posisi masing-masing** dengan adil, lengkap dengan nama dan alasan, tanpa memihak: ***So, there are two views. Rina prefers an online launch because it's cheaper; Budi would rather launch in Jakarta because the client wants an event.***
- **Usulkan:** ***So, can we agree to …?*** / ***Shall we go with option B?*** (*Shall we* lebih British; orang Amerika sering bilang ***Should we …?***) / ***I suggest we …***
- **Pastikan keputusannya:** lewat **mufakat** (semua menerima): ***Can everyone live with that?*** (= kamu bisa menerimanya, walaupun bukan pilihan favoritmu) / ***Any objections?*** Atau lewat **voting** (pemungutan suara): ***Let's put it to a vote.*** / ***Can I have a show of hands?***

Ingat dari B2: **diam bukan berarti setuju.** Kalau tidak ada yang bicara, tanya lagi, atau tanya yang pendiam dengan menyebut namanya.

rows.en: So, there are two views on this. Let me make sure I've got them right.
rows.id: Jadi, ada dua pandangan soal ini. Saya pastikan dulu saya menangkapnya dengan benar.

rows.en: So, can we agree to delay the launch by two weeks?
rows.id: Jadi, bisakah kita sepakat menunda peluncuran dua minggu?

rows.en: Shall we go with option B?
rows.id: Bagaimana kalau kita pilih opsi B?

rows.en: It's not perfect, but can everyone live with that?
rows.id: Memang tidak sempurna, tapi semuanya bisa menerima itu?

rows.en: We still don't agree, so let's put it to a vote.
rows.id: Kita masih belum sepakat, jadi mari kita voting.

rows.en: We'll aim for consensus, but if we can't agree by eleven, Bu Ani will decide.
rows.id: Kita usahakan mufakat, tapi kalau sampai jam sebelas belum sepakat, Bu Ani yang memutuskan.
rows.note: agree the decision rule at the start of the meeting

id.note: sepakati cara mengambil keputusan di awal rapat

blocks.text: **Musyawarah untuk mufakat: a strength, and when to adapt it.** Deciding by discussion until everyone agrees is a real strength: everyone is heard, the group owns the decision, and relationships stay good. International managers spend a lot of effort on the same thing (they call it *building buy-in*). But it can take several meetings, and people may say yes in public while they still disagree (sungkan). Many international teams expect a decision **in this meeting**, with a clear owner, even if not everyone loves it. The bridge: say at the start how you'll decide (***We'll aim for consensus, but if we can't agree by eleven, we'll vote.***), and check real agreement with ***Can everyone live with that?***

id.text: **Musyawarah untuk mufakat: sebuah kekuatan, dan kapan perlu menyesuaikan.** Mengambil keputusan lewat diskusi sampai semua setuju adalah kekuatan yang nyata: semua orang didengar, kelompok merasa memiliki keputusannya, dan hubungan tetap baik. Manajer internasional juga berusaha keras untuk hal yang sama (mereka menyebutnya *building buy-in*). Tapi prosesnya bisa makan beberapa kali rapat, dan orang bisa bilang setuju di depan umum padahal masih tidak setuju (sungkan). Banyak tim internasional berharap keputusan diambil **di rapat ini**, dengan penanggung jawab yang jelas, walaupun tidak semua orang menyukainya. Jembatannya: sebutkan di awal bagaimana keputusan akan diambil (***We'll aim for consensus, but if we can't agree by eleven, we'll vote.***), dan cek persetujuan yang sebenarnya dengan ***Can everyone live with that?***

blocks.prompt: After 40 minutes the group still can't agree, and the decision must be made today. You've already heard both sides. What's the best next step?
options: Let's meet again next week, and the week after, until everyone agrees.
We've heard both sides, and we need a decision today. Let's put it to a vote.
OK, I'll decide alone. No more questions, please.
blocks.explain: Both sides have been heard and there's a deadline, so a vote is a fair way to decide now. Meeting again and again ignores the deadline, and deciding alone with *No more questions* shuts the group out.

id.prompt: Setelah 40 menit kelompok masih belum sepakat, dan keputusan harus diambil hari ini. Kamu sudah mendengar kedua pihak. Apa langkah terbaik berikutnya?
id.explain: Kedua pihak sudah didengar dan ada tenggat, jadi voting adalah cara yang adil untuk memutuskan sekarang. Rapat lagi dan lagi mengabaikan tenggatnya, dan memutuskan sendiri dengan *No more questions* menutup suara kelompok.

id.title: Poin tindak lanjut dan menutup rapat

blocks.text:
A decision only matters if someone does something. Each **action point** (poin tindak lanjut) needs three parts: **who + what + by when**.
- ***Rina will send the draft by Thursday.***
- ***Budi, could you check the costs with finance by Wednesday?***

**by Thursday** = paling lambat hari Kamis (a deadline). **until Thursday** = sampai hari Kamis: something continues up to that day (*The office is closed until Thursday*).

Then close the meeting:
- ***Let's go over the action points.*** (go over = tinjau lagi)
- ***To sum up, we're going with option B, and …***
- ***Our next meeting is on Tuesday the 9th at ten.***
- ***Thanks, everyone. I'll send round the minutes this afternoon.***

id.text:
Keputusan baru berarti kalau ada yang menjalankannya. Setiap **action point** (poin tindak lanjut) butuh tiga bagian: **siapa + apa + paling lambat kapan**.
- ***Rina will send the draft by Thursday.***
- ***Budi, could you check the costs with finance by Wednesday?***

**by Thursday** = paling lambat hari Kamis (tenggat). **until Thursday** = sampai hari Kamis: sesuatu berlangsung terus sampai hari itu (*The office is closed until Thursday*).

Lalu tutup rapatnya:
- ***Let's go over the action points.*** (go over = tinjau lagi)
- ***To sum up, we're going with option B, and …***
- ***Our next meeting is on Tuesday the 9th at ten.***
- ***Thanks, everyone. I'll send round the minutes this afternoon.***

rows.en: Rina will send the draft by Thursday.
rows.id: Rina akan mengirim drafnya paling lambat hari Kamis.
rows.note: who: Rina · what: send the draft · by when: Thursday

id.note: siapa: Rina · apa: mengirim draf · paling lambat: Kamis

rows.en: Dimas will update the price list by the end of the week.
rows.id: Dimas akan memperbarui daftar harga paling lambat akhir minggu ini.

rows.en: Let's go over the action points before we finish.
rows.id: Mari kita tinjau poin tindak lanjutnya sebelum selesai.

rows.en: To sum up, we're going with option B, and the launch moves to April.
rows.id: Sebagai rangkuman, kita pilih opsi B, dan peluncurannya pindah ke bulan April.

rows.en: Our next meeting is on Tuesday the 9th at ten.
rows.id: Rapat kita berikutnya hari Selasa tanggal 9 jam sepuluh.

rows.en: Thanks, everyone. I'll send round the minutes this afternoon.
rows.id: Terima kasih, semuanya. Notulennya saya kirim sore ini.

blocks.text:
Two traps:
- **`until Thursday` ✗ for a deadline.** *Sampai Kamis* sounds like *until Thursday*, but for a deadline English says **by Thursday** (paling lambat Kamis). `Rina will send the draft until Thursday` ✗ sounds like she'll keep sending it all week.
- **Vague action points.** `We'll follow up` ✗, `Someone will check it` ✗, `ASAP` ✗: nobody knows who or when, so it often doesn't happen. Always say a name, a task and a day.

id.text:
Dua jebakan:
- **`until Thursday` ✗ untuk tenggat.** *Sampai Kamis* terdengar seperti *until Thursday*, tapi untuk tenggat bahasa Inggris memakai **by Thursday** (paling lambat Kamis). `Rina will send the draft until Thursday` ✗ terdengar seperti dia terus mengirimnya sepanjang minggu.
- **Poin tindak lanjut yang kabur.** `We'll follow up` ✗, `Someone will check it` ✗, `ASAP` ✗: tidak ada yang tahu siapa atau kapan, jadi sering tidak terjadi. Selalu sebutkan nama, tugas dan harinya.

blocks.prompt: Bu Ani needs the invoice on Friday at the latest. Which action point is correct?
options: Dimas will send the invoice until Friday.
Dimas will send the invoice by Friday.
Dimas will send the invoice at Friday.
blocks.explain: **by Friday** = paling lambat hari Jumat: a deadline. *until Friday* is for something that continues up to Friday (from Indonesian *sampai*), and days take *on*, not *at*.

id.prompt: Bu Ani butuh invoicenya paling lambat hari Jumat. Poin tindak lanjut mana yang benar?
id.explain: **by Friday** = paling lambat hari Jumat: tenggat. *until Friday* dipakai untuk sesuatu yang berlangsung terus sampai Jumat (dari bahasa Indonesia *sampai*), dan hari memakai *on*, bukan *at*.

suggestedQuestions: How do I stop a senior colleague from dominating the meeting without being rude?
What's the difference between 'by Thursday' and 'until Thursday'?
When should I call a vote instead of waiting for everyone to agree?
Does 'take it offline' mean meeting face to face?

resources.title: Chair a Meeting in English - Useful English Phrases for Meetings
resources.note: A full lesson (about 20 minutes) on chairing: starting the meeting, introducing the agenda, inviting people to speak, keeping the discussion on topic and closing. All in English, with English subtitles; it explains why each phrase works.

id.note: Pelajaran lengkap (sekitar 20 menit) tentang memimpin rapat: membuka rapat, memperkenalkan agenda, mengajak orang bicara, menjaga diskusi tetap pada topik dan menutup rapat. Seluruhnya dalam bahasa Inggris, dengan subtitle bahasa Inggris; dijelaskan juga kenapa setiap ungkapan cocok dipakai.

resources.title: Setting an agenda – English at Work
resources.note: A short, funny animated episode from the English at Work series: a team sets the agenda for a meeting, with phrases for opening, moving to the next item and closing. British English; the language is a little easier than this lesson, so it's a relaxed review.

id.note: Episode animasi pendek dan lucu dari seri English at Work: sebuah tim menyusun agenda rapat, dengan ungkapan untuk membuka, pindah ke butir berikutnya dan menutup rapat. Bahasa Inggris British; bahasanya sedikit lebih mudah dari pelajaran ini, jadi cocok untuk mengulang dengan santai.

id.intro: Di B2 kamu sudah belajar ikut serta dalam rapat: menyela dengan sopan, mengklarifikasi, merangkum dan memberi update perkembangan. Sekarang kamu yang memimpin. Kamu akan membuka rapat dan mengatur agenda, menjaga diskusi tetap adil dan fokus, meredakan perbedaan pendapat, dan mengarahkan kelompok ke keputusan yang jelas lengkap dengan poin tindak lanjutnya. Pemanasan: ingat rapat terbaik yang pernah kamu ikuti. Apa yang dilakukan orang yang memimpinnya?
suggestedQuestions: Bagaimana cara menghentikan rekan senior yang mendominasi rapat tanpa terdengar kasar?
Kapan sebaiknya saya mengadakan voting daripada menunggu semua orang setuju?
Apakah 'take it offline' berarti bertemu tatap muka?

assessment.lm-1: Kamu memimpin rapat anggaran di sebuah bank di Surabaya. Setelah menyapa semua orang, kamu menyebutkan untuk apa rapat ini. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: The ___ of today's meeting is to agree on next year's training budget.
assessment.lm-2: Rapat akan dimulai, dan seseorang perlu menulis catatan resmi tentang apa yang dibahas dan diputuskan (notulen). Minta Sari dengan sopan. Lengkapi dengan satu kata dalam bahasa Inggris: Could Sari take the ___?
assessment.lm-3: Dalam rapat tentang tata letak kantor baru di Bandung, Budi mulai membahas kenaikan gaji. Itu penting, tapi tidak ada di agenda hari ini. Lengkapi dengan satu kata (kata ini juga dipakai untuk mobil): That's a valid point, Budi, but it's not on today's agenda. Can we ___ it for now and come back to it next month?
assessment.lm-4: Dalam rapat tim, Rina dan Dimas mulai berdebat soal satu invoice dari bulan Agustus. Hanya mereka berdua yang perlu menyelesaikannya, dan delapan orang sedang menunggu. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: I can see you both feel strongly about this. Let's take that ___ and discuss it after the meeting.
assessment.lm-5: Pak Hasan butuh kontrak yang sudah ditandatangani paling lambat hari Kamis. Lengkapi poin tindak lanjutnya dengan satu kata: Budi will send Pak Hasan the signed contract ___ Thursday.
assessment.lm-6: Poin tindak lanjut ini ada di notulen rapat proyek di Jakarta: 'Budi will call the supplier about the late delivery.' Bu Ani bilang poin ini belum lengkap. Poin tindak lanjut yang baik menyebutkan siapa, apa dan paling lambat kapan. Mana yang belum ada di sini? Tulis satu kata dalam bahasa Inggris: who, what atau when.
assessment.lm-7: Di akhir rapat, kamu mengulang keputusan-keputusannya secara singkat sebelum menutup. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: To ___ up: we've chosen the venue in Bandung, Sari will book it by Friday, and our next meeting is on the 3rd.
